Subject: Initial MAP: deployment mode + region windows (HealthSync)

Evelyn / Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, the execs want a concise mutual action plan so we can lock in a procurement window and a target go-live. Our key constraints:
- Data residency preference: EU-first (GDPR controls mandatory)
- Performance: <120ms p95 for chat endpoint in EU region
- Timeline: procurement decision by 12/10 to meet Q1 launch targets

I've started a spreadsheet with evaluation criteria and proposed decision gates: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aB2cMAP-HealthSync (read-only for now).

Top question for you: given our latency and compliance needs, should we plan for Redwood Hosted in eu-1 with dedicated capacity reserve, or a Private (VPC) deployment? We need cost/lead-time tradeoffs and a prescriptive runbook for sign-offs (security review, procurement PO, infra lead readiness).

Also looping Ryan (procurement) — Ryan, what does your approval timeline look like if we have a signed MAP and an SLA addendum?

Thanks,
Marta
Director of Platform Integrations
HealthSync

Subject: Re: Initial MAP: deployment mode + region windows (HealthSync)

Thanks Marta — this is a great start. I pulled the sheet and added a proposed mutual action plan slice focused specifically on the deployment decision (see tab: Deploy-Decision). Key clarifications up front:

- Recommendation: run a short evaluation with Hosted (eu-1) with a Dedicated pool reserved for the canary week. If Hosted fails the p95 SLA in your traffic profile we will fall back to Private (VPC) onboarding with a 6-week lead time.
- Why: Hosted + Dedicated gives the fastest time-to-value and the simplest procurement flow (usage + reserved capacity amendment). Private is heavier (networking + KMS + audit) but gives stronger isolation and is useful if you require on-prem or air-gapped.
- Lead times (approx): Hosted + Dedicated reserve: 1–2 weeks to reserve capacity + 3 business days for canary config. Private (VPC) onboarding: 4–6 weeks (network, KMS, SOC evidence exchange).

Requests from our side to finalize MAP:
1) Confirm the list of deciders (name + title) and procurement PO owner by 12/03.
2) Share a redacted sample request trace (to validate sequence length / token volume) by 12/04.
3) Confirm whether HealthSync requires HSM-backed KMS — if yes, that pushes Private earlier in the plan.

I attached our SOC2 extract and a short diff of the runbook for your legal/security team.

Available times for a 30m sync this week: 12/02 11:00–11:30 PT, 12/03 08:00–09:00 PT. I can also host a technical canary rehearsal next Thursday.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
A: Redwood Inference, 480 Mission St.

Subject: Internal: healthsync deployment economics + ops runbook

Folks — quick internal note to capture numbers and a proposed ops play for the MAP:

- Traffic estimate (from Marta): steady 60 rps in EU, peak 180 rps
- Model: small-medium LLM (token profile ~ tokens/request 350 avg, 1.2M tokens/day)
- Hosted + Dedicated (eu-1) estimate: reserved pool (8x A100 equiv) + burst = ~$65k/month committed; p95 latency target feasible with our batching knobs and prefix caching.
- Private (VPC) estimate: infra/setup uplift + 1.2x unit cost, 4–6 week onboarding (network + KMS).

Operational plan to include in MAP:
1) Week 0: Sign MAP and SLA amendment (procurement PO).
2) Week 1: Reserve dedicated pool in eu-1; config canary route; send pre-canary runbook to HealthSync.
3) Week 2: Canary week (traffic mirror 10% production for 48–72h); collect token latency/cost metrics + quality evals.
4) Week 3: Decision gate: if p95 <= 120ms and quality tolerances met -> full cutover. Else -> trigger Private onboarding runbook.

I suggest we pre-authorize a 10% overage credit for canary (to avoid procurement churn). Also add a clause: customer can escalate to Private within 7 days after failed canary with a prioritized onboarding lane.

Putting Marissa and Rishi on the thread for legal / pricing sign-off.

Karthik
VP, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

– Marta

Thanks for the quick replies. Per thread and internal review, attaching the MAP slice that captures the deployment runbook and the procurement close windows. Short version / agreed actions:

1) Decision path: Start Hosted in eu-1 with Dedicated reservation -> Canary week -> Decision gate (p95 <=120ms) -> If pass: full cutover; if fail: trigger Private onboarding (4–6 week lane).
2) Procurement: HealthSync to provide PO owner and deciders by 12/03 (open), Redwood to provide itemized committed amount by 12/06.
3) Security: HealthSync to confirm HSM requirement by 12/04; Redwood to provide SOC2 evidence + SOC2-Audit-Exhibit.pdf (attached).
4) Canary observability checklist (included in runbook): token-level p95, request error rate, CPU/GPU util spikes, cost-per-inference estimates, and quality regression set (we'll run 5 canonical prompts).
5) Exec sync scheduled: 12/08 09:00–09:30 CET (tentative) — please confirm attendees.

Next immediate step for us: I will send the itemized committed cost by EOD 12/06 and the canary runbook in a short punchlist. Please confirm procurement owner's email so I can route the formal SLA addendum and MAP for signature.

Thanks,
